catalog_quote: [Costello 2014:24-25] The maximal syllable template is (C)V(C) with both the onset and the coda being optional. The only consonant that can appear in the coda is the glottal stop (ꞌ), and this consonant cannot appear in the onset. Syllables with a glottal stop in the coda appear only in the penultimate syllable. Stress falls on the penultimate syllable of polysyllabic content words; monosyllabic words (and the few bisyllabic function words) do not take stress. [Bradley 1970:13, sec. 1.25] JM has two stresses: microstress /'/ marks the center of a microsegment by means of its intensity and duration; macrostress /''/ frequently occurs instead of microstress in one microsegment of a macrosegment, has greater intensity, and marks the center of the macrosegment. [Bradley 1970:17, sec. 1.4] The syllables just described cluster together according to several well-defined patterns to form microsegments. Microsegments built according to these patterns always have a center followed by one postcenter satellite. The center consists of a tonic syllable that is oral, nasal, or checked; it must be followed by one posttonic syllable that is oral or nasal. (Such a two-syllable configuration has been called a "couplet" by Pike and associates.)

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable of polysyllabic content words. Since Mixtec content roots are bisyllabic couplets, this is the first syllable of the couplet; the glottal-stop coda is likewise restricted to that penultimate syllable. Monosyllabic words and the few bisyllabic function words are unstressed. The language is tonal (three level tones with a high/low allophone each, per Bradley 1970:13, with extensive sandhi); tone and stress are described independently.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllabic words and the few bisyllabic function words take no stress; no other exceptions given.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (content words); no statement about phrase-level stress or citation forms. Data are from the Mixtec of Santa María Jicaltepec (municipio Santiago Pinotepa Nacional), which Costello identifies with ISO mio / Ethnologue 'Pinotepa Nacional Mixtec'. The statement is a single sentence in an orthography-oriented phonology overview of an aspect/mood thesis, not a dedicated phonological analysis; Bradley 1970 (unreachable here) is the primary phonological description.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes the Mixtec of Santa María Jicaltepec (municipio Santiago Pinotepa Nacional, Oaxaca), which Costello (p. 20) equates with ISO 639-3 mio = Glottolog pino1237 'Pinotepa Nacional Mixtec' (also 'Jicaltepec Mixtec', 'Coastal Mixtec', INALI 'mixteco de Oaxaca de la costa oeste central'); MixteCoDB likewise files Santa María Jicaltepec (jica11) under pino1237. No separate glottocode exists for the Jicaltepec town variety. The unread Becerra Roldán 2018 thesis treats San Pedro Tulixtlahuaca, another town Glottolog places in pino1237.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog and Costello 2014 (stress on the first syllable of the two-syllable couplet = penultimate of the stem), but Bradley's framework adds detail: the stress domain is the microsegment (Pike's couplet), pretonic syllables (up to five) and posttonic enclitic syllables (up to four) are atonic, and there is a second degree (macrostress) at the phrase level. Because postmicrosegment enclitics are counted as atonic syllables after the couplet, stress at the level of stem+clitics is not strictly penultimate; this is compatible with Costello's restriction to content words.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word-level (micro)stress falls on the first syllable of the disyllabic couplet (tonic + exactly one posttonic syllable), i.e. on the penultimate syllable of the stem-couplet. Up to five atonic syllables may precede the couplet (premicrosegment, e.g. /sekre'tariyū/ 'secretary', /ka'rlopā/ 'wood plane') and one to four atonic syllables (mostly enclitic pronouns and particles) may follow it (postmicrosegment, p. 21, e.g. /('maa) ratara/ 'these particular men', /(ta'qárá) ra/). Macrostress, the phrase-level peak, always lands on a syllable that already bears microstress (p. 20). Stress is intensity+duration, distinct from the three-way tone contrast (sec. 1.24). Costello's 'penultimate syllable of polysyllabic content words' is the same rule seen at the word level, since content words are couplets; the catalog's 'penult regardless of length' holds only if enclitics are excluded from the word.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Two degrees: microstress (one per microsegment/couplet, the word-level stress) and macrostress (one, two or none per macrosegment/phrase; falls on a microstressed syllable and has greater intensity). No rhythmic secondary stress within words is described.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllabic morphs 'CVV / 'CV?V and CV'CVV weaken to atonic CV / CVCV when macrostress falls on another microsegment (sec. 2.2, pp. 24-25); emphatic speech style E3 delays the last stress by one syllable and lengthens the last vowel (sec. 1.27, p. 14); Spanish loans with clusters are listed with stress on the couplet, e.g. /sé'stiyā/ 'Spanish', /'sakramedū/ 'sacraments' (p. 17).
new_statements.identity_note: Both listed works are the same publication (Bradley's 1965 Cornell dissertation, published by SIL in 1970). It describes the Mixtec of Jicaltepec ("JM", ~300 adult inhabitants, informants named p. 2), the same village (Santa María Jicaltepec, municipio Pinotepa Nacional) as Costello 2014 (thesis p. 20); Glottolog pino1237 / ISO mio. Bradley's introduction also refers to a "southern dialect" and a "western dialect" of Mixtec described in his 1957 paper and Overholt 1961, but the phonology chapter is JM only.

tone_statements.citation: Becerra Roldán, Braulio. 2021. Interacciones segmentales y tonales en nominales poseídos del mixteco de Tulixtlahuaca. Anales de Antropología 55(2): 91-106.
tone_statements.quote: El sistema fonológico incluye 18 segmentos consonánticos, nueve vocálicos y tres tonos de nivel. … Con respecto a los tres tonos de nivel (A)lto, (M)edio y (B)ajo presentados en el cuadro 2, se combinan en el pie para formar las melodías tonales básicas que se presentan en el cuadro 3 … En cuanto a la unidad portadora de tono, se asume que es la mora porque, superficialmente, las sílabas ligeras del pie bisilábico solo pueden portar un tono; mientras que la sílaba pesadas del pie monosilábico puede portar dos (Yip 2002).
tone_statements.translation: The phonological system includes 18 consonantal segments, nine vocalic ones and three level tones. … As for the three level tones H(igh), M(id) and L(ow) presented in table 2, they combine within the foot to form the basic tonal melodies presented in table 3 … As for the tone-bearing unit, it is assumed to be the mora because, on the surface, the light syllables of the disyllabic foot can bear only one tone, while the heavy syllable of the monosyllabic foot can bear two (Yip 2002).
tone_statements.locator: p. 94, sec. 'Palabra mínima e inventario fonológico', text between cuadro 2 and cuadro 3 and paragraph after cuadro 3
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (high, mid, low), mora the TBU, combined into foot melodies A.A A.M A.B M.M B.M B.B; prominence on the first syllable of a bimoraic trochaic foot; phrase-level boundary high.

tone_statements.citation: Becerra Roldán, Braulio. 2018. Análisis sincrónico y consideraciones diacrónicas sobre la fonología del mixteco de San Pedro Tulixtlahuaca. Tesis de maestría, UNAM. 187 pp.
tone_statements.quote: El MT tiene tres tonos de nivel Alto, Medio y Bajo, que es el número más estándar en cuanto a tonos fonológicos se refiere, y cada uno de éstos se combinan en los morfemas para formar diferentes melodías tonales que varían según el número de tonos asociados a una base. … la mora, no la sílaba ni el segmento, es la Unidad Portadora de Tono (UPT). Lo anterior es exactamente lo que se observa en el MT. … Puesto que en el MT existen tres tonos de nivel, nueve melodías tonales son posibles; no obstante, solo ocurren seis. Además, existen melodías con un tono alto final
tone_statements.translation: Tulixtlahuaca Mixtec has three level tones, High, Mid and Low, which is the most standard number as far as phonological tones are concerned, and each of these combines within morphemes to form different tonal melodies that vary according to the number of tones associated with a base. … the mora, not the syllable or the segment, is the Tone-Bearing Unit (TBU). This is exactly what is observed in MT. … Since MT has three level tones, nine tonal melodies are possible; however, only six occur. In addition, there are melodies with a final high tone
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (High, Mid, Low) on the mora; six melodies on the bimoraic couplet plus a morpheme-final high tone giving final rises; separate intensity stress on the penult of disyllables.

tone_statements.citation: García Mejía, Griselda (2012). Las cláusulas de complemento en el tu'un²³ sa²bi³ de San Pedro Jicayán, Oaxaca. Ciudad de México: Centro de Investigaciones y Estudios Superiores en Antropologí. xvi+237 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Los tonos se marcan sobre unidades con mora. Es decir, cada segmento que aporta un peso moraico puede expresar un tono (Chávez 2010:142). El TSJ tiene tres tonos de nivel y cinco tonos de contorno en palabras léxicas. Represento los tonos con números, así: 3=tono alto, 2=tono medio, 1=tono bajo, 32=tono alto-medio, 31=tono alto-bajo, 21= tono medio-bajo, 23= tono medio-alto, y 12= tono bajo-medio. Mientras que los tonos de nivel ocurren en cualquier sílaba (mono o bimoraica), los tonos de contorno ocurren solo en sílabas bimoraicas.
tone_statements.translation: Tones are marked on units with a mora. That is, each segment that contributes moraic weight can express a tone (Chávez 2010:142). TSJ has three level tones and five contour tones in lexical words. I represent the tones with numbers: 3=high, 2=mid, 1=low, 32=high-mid, 31=high-low, 21=mid-low, 23=mid-high, 12=low-mid. While level tones occur on any syllable (mono- or bimoraic), contour tones occur only on bimoraic syllables.
tone_statements.locator: Anexo 'Una introducción a la fonología del TSJ', §5 Tonos, p. 230; inventory restated with minimal pairs pp. 231-233 and §6 p. 237; also Cap. 1 §3 p. 5 'El TSJ tiene 8 tonos'.
tone_statements.summary: Eight contrastive tones: level high, mid, low; falling high-mid, mid-low, high-low; rising mid-high, low-mid. Tone on moraic units, contours only on bimoraic syllables; tone also marks aspect, person.

tone.quote: The split of some couplets into distinct perturbation classes in Jicaltepec seems to be related to this Proto-Mixtec feature as well, although the partial merging o f some Proto-Mixtec cou- plets (basic and non-basic) in this dialect complicates the analysis. Jical- tepec morpheme classes high-high (sandhi class I) and low-low (sandhi class I) resulting from Proto-Mixtec *low-low'' and *high-high'' respec- tively contrast with high-high (sandhi class III) and low-low (sandhi class II) resulting from Proto-Mixtec * low-low and *high-high.

tone.quote: El MT tiene tres tonos de nivel Alto, Medio y Bajo, que es el número más estándar en cuanto a tonos fonológicos se refiere, y cada uno de éstos se combinan en los morfemas para formar diferentes melodías tonales que varían según el número de tonos asociados a una base. … la mora, no la sílaba ni el segmento, es la Unidad Portadora de Tono (UPT). Lo anterior es exactamente lo que se observa en el MT. … Puesto que en el MT existen tres tonos de nivel, nueve melodías tonales son posibles; no obstante, solo ocurren seis. Además, existen melodías con un tono alto final
tone.translation: Tulixtlahuaca Mixtec has three level tones, High, Mid and Low, which is the most standard number as far as phonological tones are concerned, and each of these combines within morphemes to form different tonal melodies that vary according to the number of tones associated with a base. … the mora, not the syllable or the segment, is the Tone-Bearing Unit (TBU). This is exactly what is observed in MT. … Since MT has three level tones, nine tonal melodies are possible; however, only six occur. In addition, there are melodies with a final high tone
tone.summary: Three level tones (High, Mid, Low) on the mora; six melodies on the bimoraic couplet plus a morpheme-final high tone giving final rises; separate intensity stress on the penult of disyllables.
tone.says: Three level tones (High, Mid, Low) on the mora; six melodies on the bimoraic couplet plus a morpheme-final high tone giving final rises; separate intensity stress on the penult of disyllables.

tone.quote: Los tonos se marcan sobre unidades con mora. Es decir, cada segmento que aporta un peso moraico puede expresar un tono (Chávez 2010:142). El TSJ tiene tres tonos de nivel y cinco tonos de contorno en palabras léxicas. Represento los tonos con números, así: 3=tono alto, 2=tono medio, 1=tono bajo, 32=tono alto-medio, 31=tono alto-bajo, 21= tono medio-bajo, 23= tono medio-alto, y 12= tono bajo-medio. Mientras que los tonos de nivel ocurren en cualquier sílaba (mono o bimoraica), los tonos de contorno ocurren solo en sílabas bimoraicas.
tone.locator: Anexo 'Una introducción a la fonología del TSJ', §5 Tonos, p. 230; inventory restated with minimal pairs pp. 231-233 and §6 p. 237; also Cap. 1 §3 p. 5 'El TSJ tiene 8 tonos'.
tone.translation: Tones are marked on units with a mora. That is, each segment that contributes moraic weight can express a tone (Chávez 2010:142). TSJ has three level tones and five contour tones in lexical words. I represent the tones with numbers: 3=high, 2=mid, 1=low, 32=high-mid, 31=high-low, 21=mid-low, 23=mid-high, 12=low-mid. While level tones occur on any syllable (mono- or bimoraic), contour tones occur only on bimoraic syllables.
tone.summary: Eight contrastive tones: level high, mid, low; falling high-mid, mid-low, high-low; rising mid-high, low-mid. Tone on moraic units, contours only on bimoraic syllables; tone also marks aspect, person.
tone.says: Eight contrastive tones: level high, mid, low; falling high-mid, mid-low, high-low; rising mid-high, low-mid. Tone on moraic units, contours only on bimoraic syllables; tone also marks aspect, person.
